hot.kicker: The slate includes short-form stories, stop-motion adventures and a selection of dance videos The post ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ bonus collection added to Netflix – with 78 minutes of new content appeared first on NME .
hot.author: Tom Skinner
hot.body:
Netflix has released 78 minutes of new KPop Demon Hunters bonus material. Find all the details below.
The collection comprises four seasons of extras across two companion titles, equalling 22 episodes in total.
Per What’s On Netflix , the additional content includes KPop Demon Hunters PLAYlist – a brand-new kids title that added three seasons of short-form stories, stop-motion adventures, and hands-on games on Monday (November 2).
The KPop Demon Hunters Bonus Content series has picked up a second season, too, titled ‘Dance Videos’. This runs for just under 29 minutes, and is aimed at viewers who want to learn the moves.
It boasts the recently released animated clip of HUNTR/X rehearsing a version of their viral smash ‘How It’s Done’ , as well as videos for ‘Golden’, ‘Takedown’, ‘Soda Pop’ and more.
With KPop Demon Hunters PLAYlist , fans can “play along” with their favourite characters. The show features 13 episodes, and runs for approximately 49 minutes overall. Season one – dubbed ‘HUNTR/X Backstage Pass’ – follows Rumi, Mira and Zoey behind the scenes as they deal with rival idols, writer’s block and some demons.
Season two – titled ‘KPop Toy Creations’ – is a stop-motion project that sees toy versions of the characters revisiting some of the film’s biggest moments. The third instalment – named ‘Play Games With Us’ – combines “dolls and fan challenges, with a surprising amount of ramyeon”.

warm.headline: Everything Everything fight modern life on new album ‘Poison Pop’: “It’s about this drink that kills you, but you still want it”
warm.kicker: Frontman Jonathan Higgs opens up about feeling inspired by early material, accidentally predicting a dystopian future, living in the real world, and now being the time to reject "the enshittification of everything around
warm.author: Liberty Dunworth
warm.body:
Everything Everything. Photography by Bas Van Est. Creative by Everything Everything, Raygun London and Logo design by ChaChaanTeng
Everything Everything have spoken to NME about their powerful new album ‘Poison Pop’ and opened up about being inspired by their earlier records to reject the “enshitification” of the world around them.
The British art-rockers eighth album is the follow-up to 2024’s intricate ‘ Mountainhead ’. While its predecessor saw the band hone in on abstract themes and swap out lead guitars for experimentation with synths, their new record sees Everything Everything revisit their full-throttle, punk-leaning roots, fighting the world’s urge to embrace a world of “slop”.
Born from the members looking back at their earlier days, ‘Poison Pop’ was written as the band hit the road last year to celebrate the 10th anniversary of their third album ‘Get To Heaven’ – a blistering record that predicted the rise of the alt-right.
“We didn’t want to make the same album that we had just made, but also we were busy promoting an album from 10 years ago, which was quite an undertaking,” frontman Jonathan Higgs told NME . “‘Get To Heaven’ is a very aggressive record, and I’m 10 years older now, so it was a case of being like ‘Hey, guys, remember how fucking insane we used to be?’”
“In some sense, that got us in the mood to make another fast record,” he added. “I really wanted to make it a slap-in-the-face type album. ‘Mountainhead’ was all based around a metaphor and a little bit at arm’s length, which was the intention, but this one is much more in your face. You can’t hide from it.”

warm.headline: IN EFFECT with Kernom Pedals’ David Joly
warm.kicker: The youthful Frenchmen behind breakthrough guitar pedal maker Kernom—a company founded on the motto “Never Stop Playing”—found themselves with an interesting challenge when they set out to enter the crowded “boutique ped
warm.author: James Volpe Rotondi
warm.body:
The youthful Frenchmen behind breakthrough guitar pedal maker Kernom —a company founded on the motto “Never Stop Playing”—found themselves with an interesting challenge when they set out to enter the crowded “boutique pedal” market. Their goal? To create pedals that were less about tech specs and more about creative inspiration; less about how many sounds you could pack into a single pedal, and more about the artistic fluidity of each sound.
See, in the world of guitar effects pedals—those little rectangular metal “stompboxes” that sit arrayed at the feet of nearly every electric guitar player at every show you see—there are typically two types of pedals you’re likely to encounter. One type of pedal, typically an “analog” device, focuses on doing a single thing really well, creating a certain type of echo, for example (a “delay” pedal) or maybe nailing a certain “dirty” sound made famous by a Jimmy Page or Jimi Hendrix (a “fuzz”’pedal.)
The other type—including what are known as “multi-effectors” and “effect modelers”—set out to do everything well, from echoes to fuzz to the syrupy, swirly sounds known as modulation, with limitless control over said sonics. They often do so by trading analog parts for digitally produced emulations of those same sounds. It could be argued that, to some degree, they sacrifice the richness of analog for the flexibility and range—and techy drop-down menus—of digital.

warm.headline: Bob Dylan, Wearing Hoodie, Meets Pope
warm.kicker: Not quite Heaven’s door, but close
warm.author: Jazz Monroe
warm.body:
Pope Leo XIV granted Bob Dylan a private audience at the Vatican this morning (November 4), further cementing his downtown bona fides after welcoming Patti Smith in July. Dylan, the mythically private and fuss-refusing Nobel laureate, wore a black hoodie, hood up, seemingly held aloft by a black baseball cap, for the occasion, in evidence in a photo published by the Vatican’s Dicastery for Communication. Another photo seemingly shows Dylan signing a book for His Holiness, having removed a single glove.
Although raised Jewish, Dylan converted to evangelical Christianity in 1978. He released a string of Christian albums and peppered his live show with Christian songs—astounding legions of fans and contemporaries—but dialed down the religious fervor in subsequent years, primarily expressing his accord with God through the medium of Christmas songs. In 1997, he played at a concert honoring Pope John Paul II.
Pope Leo, for his part, appears to be quite the Dylan scholar. He quoted the little-known Dylan lyric “Go Away You Bomb”—written in 1963 for an unpublished book of anti-nuclear poetry—in the preface to Unarmed and Disarming: Peace Is a Gift , an anthology of his speeches.

Before this year, the Manchester band the Durutti Column hadn’t released an album since 2010, but that hasn’t stopped its fanbase from growing. Vini Reilly’s project has inspired Harry Styles, Blood Orange, the Avalanches, and now, Four Tet—who created a hazy tech-house rework of “Your Shadow at Morning” from the Durutti Column’s 2026 album, Renascent .

Blueface feels like all the mothers of his children are "delusional" and shared messages from all three women to state his case, but Jaidyn Alexis is firing back.
On Tuesday (Nov. 3), Blueface shared alleged texts from Jaidyn, Chrisean Rock and Nevaeh Akirah on his Instagram Story, writing "delusional" over each screenshot.
In Jaidyn's alleged texts, she's trying to get Blue to leave wherever he was to meet up with her to sleep with him. In Nevaeh's alleged texts, she's telling Blue to stay away from her and their newborn son, calling him a liar and noting that Chrisean hangs out with other men so she should be allowed to as well.
"I see it's no problem for the b**ch you got tatted on u to f**k with other ni**as in ur face and u go back into hers so it shouldn't be a problem for me to do it," she wrote. "Sh*t u still gon be around."
She also called out how Blue has been moving back and forth between all of them, writing, "F**k all this rotation sh*t I rather be alone. Seriously idc."
In Rock's alleged texts, where Blue appeared to respond the most, he accuses her of being with another man and tells her to stay with him and not to call him while she's with someone else. Rock denied she was with anyone in her response.

warm.headline: Iron Maiden, Z2 Comics Make ‘Time’ For Graphic Novel
warm.kicker: The project is a new anthology that expands the science fiction universe of the band’s classic 1986 album through eight stories inspired by its eight individual tracks.
warm.author: SPIN Staff
warm.body:
Iron Maiden’s Somewhere in Time is getting a suitably futuristic 40th anniversary celebration courtesy of comics publisher Z2, which is teaming with the metal legends on Somewhere in Time: The Graphic Album . The project is a new anthology that expands the science fiction universe of the band’s classic 1986 album through eight stories inspired by its eight individual tracks.
The collection assembles a formidable roster of comics and film talent, including Steve Niles, Goran Parlov, David Dastmalchian, Corin Hardy, Leah Moore, Vincent Locke and Davide Fabbri. Comic book luminary Bill Sienkiewicz, who has also collaborated with Iron Maiden frontman Bruce Dickinson, contributes the introduction. The book is framed by a prologue and epilogue focused on Eddie, the band’s iconic mascot, written by Kelly Sue DeConnick and illustrated by Andy MacDonald. The stories explore what might have happened in the moments leading up to the creation of the album’s memorable cover image.
“It’s just a great version of Eddie. My favorite version of Eddie probably,” guitarist Adrian Smith says of the Somewhere in Time incarnation of the character. “There’s a real power there — a genuine power and menace.” Smith also participates in an in-depth interview with Phantom ’s Dave Shack, reflecting on the writing and recording of the album and the staying power of its songs.
Z2 has, naturally, made the release a collector’s proposition. Deluxe and Platinum editions arrive in a metallic Time Machine slipcase with a die-cut green acetate targeting lens, featuring cover art by Blake Armstrong. The 11-song album moves between ambient psychedelia, future folk and electrifying rock, with the pair exploring themes of freedom, transcendence and the search for a more humane world through a sound built from old-school instrumentation and layers of dubbed-out electronics.

warm.headline: Four Tet Reimagines The Durutti Column’s ‘Shadow’
warm.kicker: The remix is out now via London Records, accompanied by a visualizer.
warm.author: SPIN Staff
warm.body:
The Durutti Column’s Renascent , the U.K. group’s first studio album in more than 16 years, is already finding new life beyond its own understated arrangements. Four Tet’s Kieran Hebden has reworked “Your Shadow at Morning,” transforming the song into a nine-minute meditation that folds Vini Reilly’s signature guitar washes into crisp electronic flourishes, hazy synthesizers and a gently unfolding pulse. The remix is out now via London Records, accompanied by a visualizer.
“It’s only in the last couple of years that I learnt about the Durutti Column and explored their wonderful catalog,” Hebden says. “It’s had a big impact on me, so I was thrilled when a new album was announced. And then when I was asked to do a remix, it felt like the universe was confirming I was connected to this music.”
Renascent marks a significant new chapter for the group, whose singular blend of classical guitar, ambient minimalism, jazz and electronic experimentation has always resisted easy categorization. The album reunites Reilly with drummer and manager Bruce Mitchell and producer/multi-instrumentalist Keir Stewart, deepening a discography that has influenced generations of musicians and recently attracted new fans including Blood Orange, Harry Styles, Caroline Polachek, the Avalanches and Yung Lean.
That history will be celebrated in Manchester, England, on Nov. 19, when Stewart and Mitchell lead For Vini: The Music , a special one-night performance at Albert Hall. warm.headline: Christine And The The Queens makes funky return with new single ‘Rendez-vous Avec Toi’: “The electricity remains eternally mysterious”
warm.kicker: The French singer will return to the stage next month, promising fans "a first listen to unreleased songs from the next album" The post Christine And The The Queens makes funky return with new single ‘Rendez-vous Avec To
warm.author: Tom Skinner
warm.body:
Christine And The Queens has returned with a brand-new single – listen to ‘Rendez-vous Avec Toi’ below.
The French singer announced the funky track last week, while confirming four special underplay shows in Brussels, London, Amsterdam and Paris for next month.
“Dear comrades, I’ve missed you,” Chris wrote on social media. “Back on stage for four very special shows. A moment of live music, shared together, before the next journey begins.”
His new chapter begins today (Wednesday November 4) with the release of the groovy, disco-tinged banger ‘Rendez-vous Avec Toi’. The tune explores giving in to desire and tenderness, recalling the night lovers find each other again.
“I have a rendez-vous with you, tonight. I have obsessed about it since the morning,” Chris explained of the song. “With the devotion of someone who only waits for you, and the meaning you give to life itself by your mere presence.”
He went on: “I’ll come starred with music – the new interstellar travelling of Christine And The Queens, I did it for you. In secrecy of frequencies, in genius musicians, in New York Jazz, in Moroder Groove, I kept on obsessing about this celebration, this big night found again, and I leapt into my dream.
“Names, boxes, they never defined what we share together. The electricity remains eternally mysterious. We’ll dream together of the blue flower, of this signal that keeps pinging from another planet that we don’t even know of yet; we’ll dream peace, peace with a common story, one way bigger than the one they taught us.”

warm.headline: Queens Of The Stone Age on 2027 tour plans: “We’re going to do something that’s beyond what we’ve ever done before”
warm.kicker: Josh Homme has said the band are currently in their "third act", following the release of new album 'Perfecth' The post Queens Of The Stone Age on 2027 tour plans: “We’re going to do something that’s beyond what we’ve ev
warm.author: Tom Skinner
warm.body:
Queens of the Stone Age live at Glastonbury 2023. Credit: Andy Ford for NME
Queens Of The Stone Age have hinted at plans for their 2027 live tour, teasing “something that’s beyond what we’ve ever done before”.
Josh Homme and co. have already announced headline shows in North America and across Europe for next year, with news of a UK leg expected shortly. They’ll be showcasing their ninth and latest studio album, ‘Perfecth’ , which was released last Friday (October 30).
During an interview with NME about the record, QOTSA were asked what they had in mind for the gigs, and whether fans could expect a different vibe from their stripped-back and more theatrical ‘Catacombs’ tour .
“Well, there’s a lot to cover. I think the Catacombs have changed us forever, and so there is no going back – there’s only forward,” Homme responded.
“I think we’re going to do something that’s beyond what we’ve ever done before. We learned something about the theatrics of all that, almost Vaudeville and magic. We’re going to do something I really don’t want to talk about.”
The frontman described Queens’ current era as their “third act”, with the group being keen to remain outside their comfort zone.
“I want chaos and uncertainty. Those are moments to experiment and almost feel underwater with those emotions,” Homme told NME . “It’s the right place for that. The ‘Catacombs’ shows were terrifying to do because there was nowhere to hide. That’s exactly the sort of thing we’re looking for.”

warm.headline: Once it was a £1 hanger. Now it’s a £15 locker. Why do cloakrooms cost so much on a night out?
warm.kicker: The cost of checking your coat or bag is galloping ahead of other – also rising – prices at venues. We explain the surprisingly complex reasons why Not long ago, it cost just £2 to put a coat or a heavily stuffed tote ba
warm.author: Alice Austin
warm.body:
The cost of checking your coat or bag is galloping ahead of other – also rising – prices at venues. We explain the surprisingly complex reasons why
Not long ago, it cost just £2 to put a coat or a heavily stuffed tote bag in a cloakroom on a night out. But over the course of the 2020s, that cost has increased to more than £13 in some UK venues.
At the Outernet Live venue complex in London’s Soho, it costs £11 to put a bag in a large locker. It’s £9 at east London nightclub Fold, and if you want to retrieve something, you’ll need to pay again. At north London’s Drumsheds, the UK’s biggest nightclub, they cost up to £13.20 (though they’re reusable with no extra fee). At the Warehouse Project in Manchester, large bags must be stored at a nearby Premier Inn at £11.99 per locker. Manchester’s Co-op Live Arena has a dedicated bag storage facility which costs £15 for large bags. It’s £9.99 near the 3,000-capacity Edinburgh Playhouse and £9.90 at Testbed in Leeds. How have double-digit cloakroom costs like these been normalised?
The price rises are helping to push average spending per head on a night out from £20.95 in 2020 to £28.06 in 2026, according to Night Time Industries Association. “For years, nightlife businesses have faced relentless increases in the cost of operating, from energy and employment to taxation, business rates and supply chains,” says chief executive Michael Kill. “Many have had no choice but to pass some of those costs on to consumers simply to keep their doors open. But the reality is that consumers have now hit an affordability ceiling.”

warm.headline: Oso Oso Is Perfecting the Art of Being Themselves
warm.kicker: Is there a better hook writer in the greater emo canon right now than Jade Lilitri? There are many good and iconic hook writers in the genre, especially given the genre’s blurry borders and ample crossovers into neighbor
warm.author: Brendan Menapace
warm.body:
Is there a better hook writer in the greater emo canon right now than Jade Lilitri? There are many good and iconic hook writers in the genre, especially given the genre’s blurry borders and ample crossovers into neighboring genres. But, the thing with Oso Oso, which is fair to call a solo project for Lilitri, is that no matter which of his six albums you’re currently listening to, you know it’s going to be packed full of big hooks.
Lilitri says it’s because he’s basically been writing the same song for six albums. That’s not entirely true, or at least it’s a bit of an oversimplification and kind of a self-own. It’s not that he’s just repackaging the same riff or same chorus. It’s more that he’s continually chasing something in each of his songs and each of his albums over the years: the ideal form of Oso Oso and, therefore, by extension, the ideal artistic output and creative body of work of Jade Lilitri.
“I’m 34 years old, and just thinking about legacy or whatever,” Lilitri says. “Just, whenever I go, it’d be so cool to have a big collection of music that, if someone enjoys it, to dig through. Kind of a picture of who I was as a person.”
Yes, he’s thinking about his literal mortality as a person, but there’s also the mortality of Oso Oso, which is inextricably linked to him. If and when it’s over, he wants to feel like he pushed himself and his songs to their potential.
He’s also concerned about you, the loyal listener, making sure that you’re getting your emotional and financial investment’s worth.

warm.body:
It’s been three years since Christine and the Queens shared his last proper solo album , a 20-song record inspired by Angels in America . Now, he’s back with a new song done up two ways: in French (“Rendez-vous avec toi”) and English (“Rendez-vous in your arms”). They both come with a music video co-directed by Chris and Raphaël De Albuquerque, with choreography by Alexander Ekman. Check out both versions below.
“Rendez-vous avec toi” and “Rendez-vous in your arms” are the first preview of a still-untitled new album from Christine and the Queens, which is due out sometime this spring. It follows his 2025 EP Catching Feelings with Italo disco legend Cerrone, and his 2024 album Hopecore , released under the name Rahim Redcar.
Chris will support the new double single with four full-band shows in Europe and the UK this December. He’ll perform in Brussels, London, and Amsterdam before closing out the run with a set at Alhambra in Paris. “We will revisit a repertoire that made us grow together, and give a first listen to unreleased songs from the next album,” Chris said in press materials. “We revisit, we reinterpret, we remember, and we transcend.”

warm.headline: Dave Grohl “walked off stage and broke down in tears” after playing ‘Highway To Hell’ with AC/DC
warm.kicker: “That was one of the most full-circle moments of my entire life” The post Dave Grohl “walked off stage and broke down in tears” after playing ‘Highway To Hell’ with AC/DC appeared first on NME .
warm.author: Liberty Dunworth
warm.body:
Brian Johnson and Dave Grohl on stage together. CREDIT: Kevin Mazur/Getty Images
Dave Grohl has shared how he “walked off stage and broke down in tears” after recently playing ‘Highway To Hell’ on stage with AC/DC .
The collab came following Foo Fighters stepping in for The Pretty Reckless and opening for the rock veterans in St. Louis on September 8 – something which the frontman described as “literally a dream come true” .
While it was meant to be “for one night only”, the Aussie rock legends went on to confirm Foo Fighters as joining them for another date , as they closed out the tour at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium last month – having rescheduled it from September 25 due to severe weather.
During their headline set that same night, singer Brian Johnson revealed that Grohl had asked to join the band for their 1979 classic ‘Highway To Hell’, and brought him out to play guitar and sing.
Now, Grohl has looked back at the moment and revealed that he “broke down in tears” after he left the stage.
“It was unbelievable playing for them,” he told New Zealand radio station The Rock , going on to share what it was like to play live with the band on the second night.
“It was so crazy because my wife was on the side of the stage as we played ‘Highway To Hell’. I walked off stage and I broke down in tears, sobbing like a baby,” he added. “I was sobbing, like wailing, and I couldn’t believe it. I was, like, ‘That is one of the most full-circle moments of my entire life,’ and I will never forget it.”

warm.headline: Noel Gallagher for first solo performance since Oasis reunion as he joins line-up for Goldie’s EFG London Jazz Festival
warm.kicker: “Me and Noel Gallagher do it again… 30 years, that’s what we’ve got between us” The post Noel Gallagher for first solo performance since Oasis reunion as he joins line-up for Goldie’s EFG London Jazz Festival appeared fi
warm.author: Liberty Dunworth
warm.body:
Goldie and Noel Gallagher in 1998. CREDIT: Peter Jordan – PA Images/Getty Images
Noel Gallagher has joined the line-up for Goldie ‘s shows at EFG London Jazz Festival – marking his first solo performance since the Oasis reunion last year.
Goldie is set to host two ‘Dare To Dream’ performances at this year’s festival, which will see him perform alongside an orchestra, a choir and a variety of special guests.
Both performances take place on Saturday November 14 at 5pm and 8pm, and so far the line-up includes French-Senegalese artist anaiis, jazz drummer and producer Yussef Dayes , jazz singers Natalie Williams and Cleveland Watkiss, and Skunk Anansie ’s Skin .
Taking to social media, Goldie confirmed that Noel Gallagher will also be performing on the night, in what will be his first solo performance since playing at Y Not festival in 2024 with the High Flying Birds, ahead of Oasis making their long-awaited return the following summer.
The pair have known each other for decades, with Gallagher recording guitars for Goldie’s 1998 song ‘Temper Temper’ from ‘Saturnz Return’.
“Me and Noel Gallagher do it again,” Goldie said in a clip on Instagram, pulling Gallagher’s name out of his rolodex. “30 years, that’s what we’ve got between us. We’re here, going to Royal Festival Hall to do it all over again.”
Speaking to NME about the shows, Goldie shared: “They said this music would only last five years, 35 years later I’m still here ready to do another iconic show ‘Dare To Dream’ at the Royal Festival Hall.

Robert Smith of The Cure performs in 2026. CREDIT: Shirlaine Forrest/WireImage/Getty
Robert Smith has promised that more tour dates from The Cure are on the way for 2027, and that the setlists will be “bursting with new songs”.
The band have been on the road throughout the summer, celebrating their latest album ‘ Songs of a Lost World ’ and recently wrapping up their European and UK festival tour , which included a huge show at Manchester’s Wythenshawe Park plus Isle Of Wight , Primavera Sound Barcelona and Rock en Seine.
Now, the frontman has shared some good news with Nick Grimshaw’s BBC Radio 6 show, teasing that there are still more announcements set for 2027, including more shows and some new material.
Smith shared the message to acknowledging the band’s making the 6Music 2026 Artist of the Year shortlist, and shared that he will be adding it “to my personal music highlight list of 2026 so far”, alongside curating the Teenage Cancer Trust shows at Royal Albert Hall, joining Olivia Rodrigo for the live premiere of her song ‘What’s Wrong With Me’ , and more.
“The Cure’s last show of summer at the Rock En Seine show in Paris” also made the list, as did “pretty much every one of The Cure shows that happened in between.”
“I’m looking forward to more Cure concerts in 2027,” Smith concluded. “Of course, I’m not allowed to say where or when yet, but I’m confident they will be bursting with new songs. Watch this space…”

Ha Yun Kyung transforms into Geol Seung, a guide tasked with leading an escort convoy on an unpredictable journey. The newly released stills showcase the character in her various roles, from a tavern keeper in the marketplace to a guide for the expedition.
Geol Seung is a former tavern keeper at Cheongru, an establishment in the marketplace on Ganghwa Island. As one of the key figures connected to the sacred jewel, she joins the escort convoy at Baek Gyeol’s ( Ahn Bo Hyun ) request, accompanying the group on its mission to protect the nation.
Practical by nature, Geol Seung finds her life thrown into disarray following Baek Gyeol’s arrival. Nevertheless, she proves more than capable of surviving even among the Yabyeolcho, an elite military unit. Beneath her sly, outspoken demeanor lies a warm heart and deep Buddhist faith, revealing an unexpected side to her character.

warm.body:
Cha Ye Ryun ’s agency has released a statement addressing the school bullying allegations against her.
Recently, Cha Ye Ryun became embroiled in controversy following allegations of school violence that surfaced on October 29. At the time, a post titled “Please, the school violence perpetrator born in ’85, just stop your activities” was published on an online community.
The author of the post claimed that they had been repeatedly physically assaulted and bullied by a female actress during middle school. The allegations spread after details about the actress’s birth year and school mentioned in the post were linked to Cha Ye Ryun.
In response, her agency denied the allegations, stating that they were “completely groundless.” However, the controversy has continued as additional claims have emerged online from people claiming to be the actress’s former classmates and acquaintances.
On November 4, Cha Ye Ryun’s agency HB Entertainment released an additional statement addressing the school violence allegations, once again denying the claims and warning of legal action against those spreading false information and making malicious personal attacks.
We sincerely regret causing concern among fans who care about actress Cha Ye Ryun and the public due to the recent controversy surrounding the actress online.
We have previously stated that the claims made online regarding actress Cha Ye Ryun’s past are ‘completely groundless.’ However, we take the current situation very seriously, as unverified claims and speculation made anonymously continue to spread, with criticism even being directed at the actress’s family.

At the center is a top-ranking student from a low-income family who attends a prestigious private high school on a special scholarship and is forced to take the exam on behalf of a blackmailer who knows his secret.
The newly released stills reveal the chilling side of Nam Jae Yeop (Bae Hyeon Seong), regarded as one of the top “all-round model students” at Junggyeong High School, a prestigious private institution. His bright smile among friends perfectly embodies the image of an exemplary student, while his neatly worn school uniform and warm gaze convey an air of ease and confidence.
However, when his smile fades, Nam Jae Yeop reveals an unexpected side that creates an unsettling contrast with his usual demeanor. His cold stare and defiant posture as he looks at someone hint at the darker side hidden behind his friendly smile.
The stills also capture troubling cracks beginning to emerge in Nam Jae Yeop’s seemingly perfect life. With outstanding grades, good relationships with his peers and an ideal family background, he appears to have everything going for him. Yet beneath the pressure to maintain his flawless image, he conceals deeper insecurities and desires than anyone might expect. His wounded face, twisted with anger, hints at the turbulent changes about to engulf him.

warm.author: Trent Fitzgerald

Hip-hop is back on top in 2026. Late last year, Billboard reported that hip-hop's market share dropped from 30 percent in 2020 to 24 percent in 2025, which sparked debates among fans and critics about whether rap was losing its selling power or simply resetting.
The year proves the genre is thriving. Albums from J. Cole , A$AP Rocky and Don Toliver kicked off the new year, earning big sales numbers with their respective projects.
Not to be outdone, YoungBoy Never Broke Again dropped his 17th album, Slime Cry , on the same day as Rocky and saw the biggest sales of his career. His LP pushed 70,000 equivalent album units in its opening week.
Then, at the end of January, Don Toliver delivered his new project, Octane . The collection garnered the Houston rapper-singer his first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 chart. The set earned an impressive 162,000 equivalent album units, which is his best first-sales week ever in his career.
Meanwhile, J. Cole's magnum opus, The Fall-Off , moved 280,000 equivalent album units in its first week of release.
In May, Drake scored the highest album sales among rappers this year. Drizzy's ninth studio release, Iceman , premiered at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart after moving 463,000 equivalent album units during its seven-day sales period following a May 15 launch. It marks the second-largest sales week of 2026 for an album and the biggest week of the year for a hip-hop project.

cold.headline: Takeoff Murder Trial Scheduled for Next Year
cold.author: Trent Fitzgerald
cold.body:
The trial for the man accused of killing Takeoff has been rescheduled for next year.
According to court documents obtained by XXL on Tuesday (Nov. 3), the Takeoff murder trial is now scheduled to begin on April 15, 2027. Patrick Xavier Clark, the man accused of murdering the late Migos rapper, was initially set to stand trial on Thursday (Nov. 5).
"Both sides had numerous trial conflicts and the state recently turned over a large amount of evidence that had not been seen by Mr. Clark's previous counsel," Clark's attorney, Kent Schaffer, told XXL . "While there is nothing harmful in that evidence, we still need time to review it. We still fully expect to prevail."
It's been four years since Takeoff was shot and killed outside a Houston bowling alley on Nov. 1, 2022. According to prosecutors, gunfire erupted during an argument among several men who were playing dice in the lobby of 810 Billiards & Bowling venue. Takeoff was an innocent bystander and neither participated in the dice game nor was involved in the dispute. Nevertheless, authorities said Takeoff was shot in the head and pronounced dead at the scene. Authorities identified Clark, a local DJ, as the shooter through surveillance video. Clark has pleaded not guilty and is out on a $1 million bond.
In June of 2023, Takeoff's mother, Titania Davenport, filed a wrongful death lawsuit against 810 Billiards & Bowling. The wrongful death case was settled in December of 2025 for an undisclosed sum. Now Takeoff's parents are in court battling over how to divide the payout received from the wrongful death lawsuit over their son's 2022 murder. The judge has not yet ruled in the matter.

The Detroit techno pioneer, who has died aged 64 , blended funk and electronics with information-age philosophy to create music of huge power and influence
Juan Atkins, the originator of techno who died on 31 October, spent his lifetime translating a fascination with the future into sound.
He was the oldest of the founding fathers of techno known as the “Belleville Three”, along with his junior high school friends Kevin Saunderson and Derrick May. He was the first of the trio to buy a Korg MS-10 synthesiser, and also taught the others how to DJ on turntables. His work in the duo Cybotron alongside Rik Davis was the sonic blueprint that sketched out what later became known as techno – indeed, he is the one who gave the genre its name. Without Atkins, and the way he empowered those around him, electronic music certainly would not exist in its current form today.
After moving from his birthplace of Detroit to nearby Belleville, Michigan, Atkins holed himself up in his bedroom, toiling away for hours creating drum kicks. “I more or less knew I was doing stuff that was not the normal thing to do,” he said in a Red Bull Music Academy interview in 2017 .

After pleading the Fifth last week, Yella Beezy 's childhood friend got on the stand today and admitted that he lied in grand jury testimony that eventually led to the rapper's indictment in his murder-for-hire case.
On Monday (Nov. 2), during Day 4 in Yella Beezy's murder-for-hire trial, the Dallas rapper's friend and rap associate, Theodore Thomas, a.k.a. rapper Jose Bodega, took the stand as a hostile witness under an immunity agreement to address statements he previously made to a Dallas County grand jury in February of 2025. Days before, Thomas repeatedly invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination and refused to answer any questions.
However, under duress, Thomas answered questions from both the prosecution and defense about which of his statements were truthful and which were allegedly false. As reported by WFAA ABC8, prosecutors presented transcripts of Thomas' previous grand jury testimony, in which he talked about Beezy's alleged involvement in Mo3's murder. But the 34-year-old rapper said that his previous statements to the grand jury were not true.
"I told you I lied already, so asking me questions from a paper, it's like you making me re-lie," Thomas testified.
The prosecutor questioned Thomas about his previous testimony that Kewon White , the gunman who shot and killed Mo3, was paid $40,000 to carry out the hit by Yella Beezy and Trapboy Freddie.
"Y'all talked about the money, how much Kewon paid to do this, and your answer was supposedly $40,000? That was your answer," the prosecutor said.

cold.headline: ‘They said we incited riots’: explosive punks Bad Brains on drugs, self-destruction and recording from jail
cold.kicker: Young, black and fuelled by self-help mantras, they were reputedly the best live band on Earth. As their wild first sessions are rereleased, the group talk about scaring club owners – and getting kicked out of the UK Old
cold.author: Alex Deller
cold.body:
Young, black and fuelled by self-help mantras, they were reputedly the best live band on Earth. As their wild first sessions are rereleased, the group talk about scaring club owners – and getting kicked out of the UK
O ld punks might not agree on much – who was first, who was fastest, where to file the Faith/Void split LP in their record collection – but for those who saw them in their prime, Bad Brains were, unequivocally, the best live band on the planet. YouTube footage bears this out: frontman HR, born Paul D Hudson, is equal parts straining sinew and raw electricity as he bucks and contorts, punctuating rapid-fire snarls and otherworldly croons with impeccably timed backflips. The band surge around him, forging blisteringly fast punk informed by everything from the Damned and Dead Boys to P-Funk, Stevie Wonder and Chick Corea’s Return to Forever.
Young, black and fuelled by an ideology that united the 1930s self-help mantras of Napoleon Hill with Rastafari, they were outliers in the already outre 70s punk scene. But while Bad Brains helped change the face of American punk as it morphed into hardcore in the early 80s, and inspired artists as diverse as Rage Against the Machine, Deftones, Lil Jon, the Roots and Beastie Boys, defeat was never far from glory as they balanced feted live performances and a scintillating run of records with an excruciating capacity for self-sabotage.
